test_title: PYST 08: SSC Stenographer 2025: English Language & Comprehension (Held On: 08 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Choose the correct sequence to form a meaningful sentence:

(A) playing

(B) children

(C) were

(D) in the park
solution:
The correct answer is **Option (3)** i.e. **BCAD**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] ** __Key Points__ ** 

__
 
• The sentence begins with the subject "children," which is correctly indicated by **part (B).**
 
• Following the subject, "were" **(BC)** continues the logical sequence, making it clear what the children were doing.
 
• **The next part,** "playing in the park," continues the sentence logically, indicated by (CAD).
 
• **Ending with **"in the park" (D) completes the meaningful sentence by specifying the location.

Therefore, the correct answer is **BCAD.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] ** Additional Information__ ** 

 
• **Option 1 (CBAD):** This option starts with "were children playing in the park," which makes the sentence grammatically incorrect.
 
• **Option 2 (BDCA):** This option starts with "children playing were in the park," which disrupts the logical flow.
 
• **Option 4 (BACD):** This option starts with "children were playing in the park," which makes sense but skips the proper sequence.
